title: Outside-household medical support is more common alongside cost-related care foregoing

observations.period: 2025; respondents with any cost-related care foregoing
observations.method: Any Yes among E1_a-E1_e defines listed care foregoing; FS21_c=Yes defines outside-household help for medical expenses, debt, or health insurance; outcomes use single-year weight.
observations.uncertainty: Same-respondent cross-sectional comparison; no transfer amount, timing, giver, conditions, causal direction, or replicate-weight standard errors.
observations.subgroup: Respondents reporting any listed care type skipped because of cost.
observations.counterinterpretation: Outside help may be a protective alternative, a consequence of already-borne medical strain, or both; it does not prove that care was obtained or debt resolved.

observations.period: 2025; respondents with no listed cost-related care foregoing
observations.method: All E1_a-E1_e=No defines no listed care foregoing; FS21_c=Yes defines outside-household help for medical expenses, debt, or health insurance; outcomes use single-year weight.
observations.uncertainty: Same-respondent cross-sectional comparison; no transfer amount, timing, giver, conditions, causal direction, or replicate-weight standard errors.
observations.subgroup: Respondents reporting no listed care type skipped because of cost.
observations.counterinterpretation: No listed foregoing does not prove absence of unmet need, affordability pressure, or outside support for other health costs.

observations.period: 2025; insured respondents with any cost-related care foregoing
observations.method: Any Yes among E4_a-E4_f defines insured status; any Yes among E1_a-E1_e defines care foregoing; FS21_c=Yes defines outside-household help; outcomes use single-year weight.
observations.uncertainty: Coverage-conditioned same-respondent cross-sectional comparison; no transfer amount, timing, giver, conditions, causal direction, or replicate-weight standard errors.
observations.subgroup: Insured respondents reporting any listed care type skipped because of cost.
observations.counterinterpretation: Coverage and outside support can coexist with substantial unmet need and debt; this is not an insurance effect estimate.

observations.period: 2025; insured respondents with no listed cost-related care foregoing

observations.uncertainty: Coverage-conditioned same-respondent cross-sectional comparison; no transfer amount, timing, giver, conditions, causal direction, or replicate-weight standard errors.
observations.subgroup: Insured respondents reporting no listed care type skipped because of cost.
observations.counterinterpretation: No listed foregoing does not prove no unmet need or absence of outside support for other health costs.

observations.period: 2025; uninsured respondents with any cost-related care foregoing
observations.method: All E4_a-E4_f=No defines uninsured status; any Yes among E1_a-E1_e defines care foregoing; FS21_c=Yes defines outside-household help; outcomes use single-year weight.
observations.uncertainty: Coverage-conditioned same-respondent cross-sectional comparison; the uninsured cell is smaller and has no transfer amount, timing, giver, conditions, causal direction, or replicate-weight standard errors.
observations.subgroup: Uninsured respondents reporting any listed care type skipped because of cost.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lower outside-help prevalence than the insured skipping group does not imply lower burden; access to support may itself be unequal.
